findings.title: Remembering relays testimony across silence
findings.claim: The narrator's command repairs threatened self-erasure and carries testimony through media that remain available when Mary's own tongue does not.
findings.mechanism: The opening recovery-and-record command answers a later wish to become forgotten. Mary's tongue is then restrained, gesture replaces direct speech, and the book recurs in the child's declaration; testimony is preserved by transferring it across memory, text, gesture, and another voice.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening command becomes a durable relay for a scene whose central witness later cannot speak directly.
findings.containment: The trace supports a reparative relay, not a claim that every later communication is caused by the focus command. The exact context surfaces are reliable contact evidence, while unresolved branch identities remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic anchor surfaces, word coordinates, and focus returns are supplied, but the relay and its unresolved context branch roles come from a legacy-unbound trace without target morphology.

findings.title: The boundary permits social return
findings.claim: The initial withdrawal reads as a provisional boundary before re-entry under scrutiny, with Mary retaining agency over the channel of response.
findings.mechanism: Departure from the family is followed by arrival to her people while visibly carrying the child, then by a chosen gesture that redirects the demanded answer. The boundary is therefore provisional: it enables a difficult social return while preserving agency over the mode of response.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can track a circuit from departure to return without treating privacy as permanent severance.
findings.containment: The trace supports a bounded social circuit, but it does not prove that the return was voluntary or that the initial withdrawal was planned for this later scrutiny. Unresolved branches remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: Exact 19:16, 19:27, and 19:29 coordinates and focus returns are supplied, but the social-circuit reclassification comes from a legacy-unbound trace without target morphology for several context branches.

findings.title: Withdrawal reverses abandonment imagery
findings.claim: Exploratorily, Mary's self-displacement prefigures an anti-abandonment pattern: she withdraws with the child and later bears him back rather than casting him away.
findings.mechanism: The focus withdrawal root carries an anomalous cast-away-child image. When the root recurs with the child as companion and is followed by visible carrying back to the group, inward bearing and return redirect the image from abandonment toward protective accompaniment.
findings.reader_payoff: The outlier gives the repeated withdrawal a sharp ethical contrast: removal from the group does not become disposal of the child.
findings.containment: This is surprising because the cast-away-child branch is nominal and form-distant from Mary's reflexive withdrawal, so it must not be offered as the lexical translation of word 6. It remains anchored in the exact withdrawal root and becomes live only when that root recurs with the child as companion, followed by visible carrying back to the group; it is exploratory reversal imagery.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT root coordinates and focus return are supplied, but the outlier deliberately uses a nominal, form-distant branch and therefore remains a legacy-unbound exploratory relation rather than a lexical reading.
